# Events

> Events emitted by the FunctionalCalendar component and what each one passes.

Listen with `@name` in the template. Event names are camelCase, so write `@dayClicked` or `v-on:dayClicked`. In-DOM templates fold attribute names to lowercase and miss them, so use string templates or single-file components.

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Event
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Payload
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Fires when
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        input
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      calendar object
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The selection or the displayed month changes. This powers <code>
        v-model
      </code>
      
      .
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        dayClicked
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      day object
    </td>
    
    <td>
      A user clicks any day, even a disabled one or in a calendar with no selection mode.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        choseDay
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      day object
    </td>
    
    <td>
      A click changed the selection. It does not fire for disabled days, days outside <code>
        limits
      </code>
      
       or calendars with no selection mode.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        selectedDaysCount
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        Number
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      A range is complete. The payload is the number of days between start and end, not counting the first day.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        dayMouseOver
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        String
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The pointer enters a day. The payload is the day's date.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        changedMonth
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        Date
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The month changes through the arrows or the month picker.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        changedYear
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        Date
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The year changes through the arrows or the year picker.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        opened
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      none
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The calendar becomes visible.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        closed
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      none
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The calendar hides. Only modal calendars hide.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`opened` and `closed` also fire once on mount with the initial state. An inline calendar emits `opened`, and a modal calendar emits `closed`.

## Day object

`dayClicked` and `choseDay` pass an object like this:

```js
{
    day: 17,
    date: '17/10/2026',
    hide: false,
    isMouseToLeft: false,
    isMouseToRight: false,
    isHovered: false,
    isDateRangeStart: false,
    isDateRangeEnd: false,
    hideLeftAndRightDays: false,
    isToday: false,
    isMarked: false
}
```

With `with-time-picker` on a date range, `date` carries a time suffix such as `17/10/2026 00:00`.

## Example

```vue
<template>
    <FunctionalCalendar
        v-model="calendarData"
        :is-date-range="true"
        @selectedDaysCount="days = $event"
        @changedMonth="onChangedMonth"
    />
</template>

<script>
import { FunctionalCalendar } from 'vue-functional-calendar'

export default {
    components: { FunctionalCalendar },
    data() {
        return {
            calendarData: {},
            days: 0
        }
    },
    methods: {
        onChangedMonth(date) {
            console.log(date.getMonth() + 1)
        }
    }
}
</script>
```


# Examples

> Common calendar setups for Vue Functional Calendar 2.x, ready to copy.

Each example assumes `calendarData: {}` in `data()` and the component registered. The default `date-format` is `dd/mm/yyyy hh:MM`, and values drop the time unless the time picker is on, so dates read like `17/10/2026`.

## Single date

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar v-model="calendarData" :is-date-picker="true" />
```

Read `calendarData.selectedDate`.

## Date range with limits

Users can pick only inside October to December, and ranges between 2 and 14 days.

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar
    v-model="calendarData"
    :is-date-range="true"
    :limits="{ min: '1/10/2026', max: '31/12/2026' }"
    :min-sel-days="2"
    :max-sel-days="14"
    :can-clear-range="true"
/>
```

## Several ranges

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar
    v-model="calendarData"
    :is-date-range="true"
    :is-multiple-date-range="true"
    :can-clear-range="true"
/>
```

Read `calendarData.multipleDateRange`.

## Several single dates

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar v-model="calendarData" :is-multiple-date-picker="true" />
```

Read `calendarData.selectedDates`.

## Two calendars side by side

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar
    v-model="calendarData"
    :is-date-range="true"
    :is-multiple="true"
    :calendars-count="2"
    :is-layout-expandable="true"
/>
```

Add `:is-separately="true"` to let each calendar change month on its own.

## Modal range with inputs

The calendar opens when the inputs gain focus, and closes after a full range.

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar
    v-model="calendarData"
    :is-modal="true"
    :is-date-range="true"
    :is-auto-closeable="true"
    :change-month-function="true"
    :change-year-function="true"
    :date-format="'dd/mm/yyyy'"
/>
```

## Date with time

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar
    v-model="calendarData"
    :is-modal="true"
    :is-date-picker="true"
    :with-time-picker="true"
    :display-time-input="true"
    :active-minutes="[0, 15, 30, 45]"
    date-format="dd/mm/yyyy hh:mm"
/>
```

Read `calendarData.selectedDateTime`, `selectedHour` and `selectedMinute`.

## Disable dates and weekdays

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar
    v-model="calendarData"
    :is-date-picker="true"
    :disabled-dates="['beforeToday', '24/12/2026', '25/12/2026']"
    :disabled-day-names="['Sa', 'Su']"
/>
```

To allow only a list of dates, use `:enabled-dates` instead.

## Mark dates with a class

```vue
<template>
    <FunctionalCalendar v-model="calendarData" :marked-dates="markedDates" />
</template>

<script>
export default {
    data() {
        return {
            calendarData: {},
            markedDates: [
                { date: '17/10/2026', class: 'has-meeting' },
                { date: '24/10/2026', class: 'has-deadline' }
            ]
        }
    }
}
</script>

<style>
.has-meeting {
    background: #dbeafe;
}
.has-deadline {
    background: #fee2e2;
}
</style>
```

## Highlight a span

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar
    v-model="calendarData"
    :marked-date-range="{ start: '5/10/2026', end: '9/10/2026' }"
/>
```

Pass an array of `{ start, end }` objects to highlight more than one span.

## Custom day content

```vue
<template>
    <FunctionalCalendar v-model="calendarData" :is-date-picker="true">
        <template v-slot:default="props">
            <div class="custom-day">
                {{ props.day.day }}
                <small v-if="eventsByDate[props.day.date]">
                    {{ eventsByDate[props.day.date] }}
                </small>
            </div>
        </template>
    </FunctionalCalendar>
</template>

<script>
export default {
    data() {
        return {
            calendarData: {},
            eventsByDate: {
                '17/10/2026': 'Demo',
                '24/10/2026': 'Release'
            }
        }
    }
}
</script>
```

## Translate names

```js
Vue.use(FunctionalCalendar, {
    dayNames: ['Lu', 'Ma', 'Me', 'Je', 'Ve', 'Sa', 'Di'],
    monthNames: [
        'Janvier', 'Février', 'Mars', 'Avril', 'Mai', 'Juin',
        'Juillet', 'Août', 'Septembre', 'Octobre', 'Novembre', 'Décembre'
    ],
    shortMonthNames: [
        'Janv', 'Févr', 'Mars', 'Avr', 'Mai', 'Juin',
        'Juil', 'Août', 'Sept', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Déc'
    ]
})
```

## Dark theme

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar v-model="calendarData" :is-date-picker="true" :is-dark="true" />
```


# Props

> Every prop of the FunctionalCalendar component, with type, default and behavior.

Props use camelCase in JavaScript and kebab-case in templates, so `isDatePicker` becomes `is-date-picker`. A prop you leave out keeps the default shown here.

## Value and configuration

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Prop
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Type
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Default
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Description
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        value
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        Object
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      none
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The calendar state. Bind it with <code>
        v-model
      </code>
      
      . Change it from outside to preselect dates.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        configs
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        Object
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      none
    </td>
    
    <td>
      All options as one object. When set, the calendar skips every individual prop that has a <code>
        configs
      </code>
      
       key.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        newCurrentDate
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        Date
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      today
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The month to show first.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### configs

Any option in the tables below can be a key of `configs`, except `value`, `newCurrentDate`, `canClearRange`, `displayTimeInput`, `activeHours`, `activeMinutes`, `borderColor`, `alwaysUseDefaultClasses` and `configs` itself. Those keep working as props next to `configs`.

Any other prop you pass next to `configs` is ignored. Four options are also read straight from the prop in parts of the component: `isMultipleDateRange`, `showWeekNumbers`, `isSeparately` and `changeYearStep`. Set each of these in `configs` and as a prop.

```js
{
    isDateRange: true,
    sundayStart: true,
    limits: { min: '1/10/2026', max: '31/12/2026' }
}
```

## Date format

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Prop
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Type
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Default
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Description
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        dateFormat
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        String
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        dd/mm/yyyy hh:MM
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The format of every date string.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        placeholder
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        String
      </code>
      
       or <code>
        Boolean
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      the date format
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Placeholder of the date inputs in modal mode.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Use `dd`, `mm` and `yyyy` joined by `/`, `-` or `.`. Add a time part after a space: `HH:MM`, `HH:mm`, `hh:MM` or `hh:mm`. Any other time part fails prop validation.

    </td>

      Open a year picker when users click the year title.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        changeMonthStep
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        Number
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        1
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Months to move on each arrow click.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        changeYearStep
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        Number
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        3
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Years to move on each arrow click inside the year picker.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

## Example

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar
    v-model="calendarData"
    :is-date-range="true"
    :is-multiple="true"
    :calendars-count="2"
    :limits="{ min: '1/10/2026', max: '31/12/2026' }"
    :disabled-day-names="['Sa', 'Su']"
    :min-sel-days="2"
    :max-sel-days="14"
    :can-clear-range="true"
/>
```


# Slots

> Replace the day cell, navigation arrows, footer and inputs of the calendar.

Use the `v-slot` syntax from Vue 2.6.

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Slot
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Props
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Replaces
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        default
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        week
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        day
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The content of each day cell.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        navigationArrowLeft
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      none
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The previous-month arrow.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        navigationArrowRight
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      none
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The next-month arrow.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        cleaner
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      none
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The Clear Range button in the footer.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        footer
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      none
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Extra footer content, shown next to the cleaner.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        dateRangeInputs
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        startDate
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        endDate
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        isTypeable
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The two inputs of a modal date range.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        datePickerInput
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        selectedDate
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        isTypeable
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The input of a modal date picker.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The footer renders when `can-clear-range` is on or the `footer` slot is filled.

## Day slot

`day` is the [day object](https://manukminasyan.github.io/vue-functional-calendar/v2/essentials/events#day-object) and `week` holds the days of the row. When you fill the slot, the default `vfc-span-day` class no longer applies to the cell. Add `always-use-default-classes` to keep it.

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar v-model="calendarData" :is-date-picker="true">
    <template v-slot:default="props">
        <div class="custom-day">
            {{ props.day.day }}
            <span v-if="props.day.isToday" class="dot"></span>
        </div>
    </template>
</FunctionalCalendar>
```

## Arrows

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar v-model="calendarData">
    <template v-slot:navigationArrowLeft>
        <span>Prev</span>
    </template>
    <template v-slot:navigationArrowRight>
        <span>Next</span>
    </template>
</FunctionalCalendar>
```

## Footer

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar ref="calendar" v-model="calendarData" :is-date-range="true" :is-modal="true">
    <template v-slot:cleaner>
        <button type="button">Reset</button>
    </template>
    <template v-slot:footer>
        <button type="button" @click="$refs.calendar.showCalendar = false">Apply</button>
    </template>
</FunctionalCalendar>
```

A click anywhere in the `cleaner` slot clears the selected range.

## Inputs

These slots apply to modal calendars only. The slot props are read-only, so the examples bind them with `:value`.

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar v-model="calendarData" :is-date-range="true" :is-modal="true">
    <template v-slot:dateRangeInputs="props">
        <input :value="props.startDate" placeholder="Check in" readonly />
        <input :value="props.endDate" placeholder="Check out" readonly />
    </template>
</FunctionalCalendar>
```

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar v-model="calendarData" :is-date-picker="true" :is-modal="true">
    <template v-slot:datePickerInput="props">
        <input :value="props.selectedDate" placeholder="Pick a date" readonly />
    </template>
</FunctionalCalendar>
```


# Installation

> Install Vue Functional Calendar 2.x and register it in a Vue 2 app.

Vue Functional Calendar 2.x needs Vue 2.6 or later, because scoped slots and the compiled bundle use the 2.6 slot syntax. For Vue 3, use the 3.x line.

## Install

<code-group>

```bash [npm]
npm install vue-functional-calendar@^2.10.0 --save
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add vue-functional-calendar@^2.10.0
```

</code-group>

The package bundles its own styles. There is no CSS file to import.

## Register globally

`Vue.use` registers the `FunctionalCalendar` component in every template. The second argument sets defaults for every calendar.

```js
import Vue from 'vue'
import FunctionalCalendar from 'vue-functional-calendar'

Vue.use(FunctionalCalendar, {
    dayNames: ['Mo', 'Tu', 'We', 'Th', 'Fr', 'Sa', 'Su']
})
```

Global options accept any key of the [`configs`](https://manukminasyan.github.io/vue-functional-calendar/v2/essentials/props#configs) object.

## Register in a component

```js
import { FunctionalCalendar } from 'vue-functional-calendar'

export default {
    components: {
        FunctionalCalendar
    }
}
```

## Use from a CDN

The UMD build exposes a `FunctionalCalendar` global.

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/vue@2"></script>
<script src="https://unpkg.com/vue-functional-calendar@2"></script>

<div id="app">
    <functional-calendar v-model="calendarData" :is-date-picker="true"></functional-calendar>
</div>

<script>
    Vue.use(FunctionalCalendar)

    new Vue({
        el: '#app',
        data: {
            calendarData: {}
        }
    })
</script>
```

## TypeScript

The package ships `index.d.ts`. Both the named export and the default plugin export are typed.


# Usage

> Render a calendar, read the selected value and configure it with props or a configs object.

## Basic calendar

Bind the calendar with `v-model`. The bound object holds the whole calendar state.

```vue
<template>
    <FunctionalCalendar v-model="calendarData" />
</template>

<script>
import { FunctionalCalendar } from 'vue-functional-calendar'

export default {
    components: { FunctionalCalendar },
    data() {
        return {
            calendarData: {}
        }
    }
}
</script>
```

Without a selection mode, the calendar only displays dates. Turn on one mode to let users pick.

## Selection modes

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Prop
    </th>
    
    <th>
      What users pick
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        is-date-picker
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      One date.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        is-multiple-date-picker
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Any number of single dates.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        is-date-range
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      One range with a start and an end.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        is-multiple-date-range
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Several ranges, together with <code>
        is-date-range
      </code>
      
      .
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar v-model="calendarData" :is-date-range="true" />
```

## Read the selected value

`v-model` receives an object. Which keys matter depends on the mode.

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Mode
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Where the value lives
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      Date picker
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        selectedDate
      </code>
      
      , a string in <code>
        date-format
      </code>
      
      . With the time picker, also <code>
        selectedDateTime
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        selectedHour
      </code>
      
       and <code>
        selectedMinute
      </code>
      
      .
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Multiple date picker
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        selectedDates
      </code>
      
      , an array of <code>
        { date, dateTime, hour, minute }
      </code>
      
       objects.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Date range
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        dateRange.start
      </code>
      
       and <code>
        dateRange.end
      </code>
      
      , both strings.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Multiple date range
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        multipleDateRange
      </code>
      
      , an array of <code>
        { start, end }
      </code>
      
       objects.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`currentDate` is a `Date` for the month on display.

```js
{
    currentDate: new Date(2026, 9, 17),
    selectedDate: false,
    selectedDateTime: false,
    selectedHour: '00',
    selectedMinute: '00',
    selectedDatesItem: '',
    selectedDates: [],
    dateRange: { start: '3/10/2026', end: '9/10/2026' },
    multipleDateRange: []
}
```

Dates follow `date-format`, which defaults to `dd/mm/yyyy hh:MM`. Values the calendar produces drop the time part unless the time picker is on, so `selectedDate` reads `17/10/2026`. Days and months have no leading zero.

## Configure with props

Pass any option as a prop. Use kebab-case in templates.

```vue
<FunctionalCalendar
    v-model="calendarData"
    :is-date-picker="true"
    :sunday-start="true"
    date-format="dd/mm/yyyy"
    @changedMonth="onChangedMonth"
    @changedYear="onChangedYear"
/>
```

## Configure with an object

The `configs` prop takes the same options as one object. This suits shared or stored settings.

```vue
<template>
    <FunctionalCalendar v-model="calendarData" :configs="calendarConfigs" />
</template>

<script>
export default {
    data() {
        return {
            calendarData: {},
            calendarConfigs: {
                sundayStart: false,
                dateFormat: 'dd/mm/yyyy',
                isDatePicker: false,
                isDateRange: true
            }
        }
    }
}
</script>
```

<warning>

When `configs` is set, the calendar skips the props merge, so every option prop passed next to `configs` is ignored. Four options are also read straight from the prop in parts of the component: `isMultipleDateRange`, `showWeekNumbers`, `isSeparately` and `changeYearStep`. Set each of these in `configs` and as a prop.

</warning>

Option precedence, lowest to highest: built-in defaults, options given to `Vue.use`, then `configs` or individual props.
